llm.summary: This is a real browser automation skill, but it gives an agent broad default access to live browser sessions, cookies, storage, and page code execution.

dimensions.detail: For trusted local automation the browser and network authority are expected, but the default mode grants credentialed browser requests, file upload/download paths, and direct session manipulation to any authorized caller of the skill.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package has a normal Node layout, no install script, and a single declared dependency on playwright-core; I found no hidden installer, obfuscated bootstrap, or unrelated persistence mechanism.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The docs warn to use it only in trusted local environments, but the default instructions still expose raw eval/run-code and first-class cookie/storage commands without per-origin scoping or per-operation user confirmation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The daemon intentionally persists browser state across commands and supports exporting/importing live cookies and localStorage; safe mode and path confinement mitigate this, but they are optional and exported credential files are not encrypted or permission-hardened by the implementation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The browser automation purpose is coherent with Playwright control, snapshots, clicks, form filling, downloads, and advanced page scripting, and the main SKILL.md prominently discloses eval, run-code, persistent daemon state, and cookie/localStorage access.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only for trusted, local, user-visible browser automation. Start the daemon with PW_BROWSER_SAFE_MODE=1 when you do not explicitly need eval, run-code, cookies, or storage commands; do not let untrusted agents or prompts use it against logged-in accounts. Treat any exported cookies or localStorage files as passwords, delete them when done, and avoid --unsafe paths.
llm.findings:
[LP3] unexpected: The high-risk capabilities are explicitly disclosed in SKILL.md, so this is not hidden, but the broad default browser/session authority lacks an enforced least-privilege permission boundary.
[SDI-1] unexpected: package.json under-describes the sensitive behavior compared with SKILL.md and README content; this is metadata under-disclosure, not evidence of deception because the agent-facing docs are direct about the risks.
[SDI-4] expected: run-code intentionally exposes a Playwright page object. That fits an advanced automation tool, but the VM sandbox does not reduce the page/session authority, so it remains a material review concern.
[SDI-4] expected: The element-scoped eval implementation is part of the disclosed page-context code execution feature; the fragility noted by the scanner is a quality/security-reasoning concern, not a separate malicious behavior.
[PE3] expected: Cookie and storage access is intentionally implemented and documented, including safe-mode blocking and path confinement. It is purpose-aligned but high-impact because it can expose reusable session credentials by default.
[RA2] expected: The quickstart explicitly teaches session export/import and warns that the files are full authenticated sessions. The behavior is disclosed, but default session persistence remains a material concern for agent use.
[RA2] expected: README.en.md documents cookie/localStorage persistence, credential risk, cleanup, and safe mode. This supports a Review verdict rather than malicious classification.
[TM1] expected: The documented --unsafe path override and direct credential commands are expected for the stated session-backup feature, but they broaden misuse potential if an untrusted or compromised agent can call the skill.
